theory.intro: When a problem mixes grams, kilograms and tonnes, first convert everything to one unit, then add, subtract or compare.
facts: Choose **one** common unit before calculating — usually the smallest in the problem.
Convert the answer back to a sensible unit at the end if needed.
steps: Pick a common unit for all the masses, using the unit requested when convenient.
Convert each mass to that unit before adding, subtracting or comparing.
For equal groups, multiply to find their total mass or divide to share the mass equally.
For an unknown equal mass, subtract the other known masses from the total, then divide by the number of equal objects.
Compare the total load with its limit, or multiply the total mass by the cost per unit when asked. State the answer with its unit.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Find the total mass of $735\text{ g}$ and $2.18\text{ kg}$ in kilograms.
(b) A $4.6\text{ kg}$ bag has $825\text{ g}$ removed. What mass remains?
(c) Which is heavier: $2.43\text{ kg}$ or $2385\text{ g}$? Find the difference in grams.

(a) A box of mass $240\text{ g}$ holds $9$ bags, each of mass $375\text{ g}$. Find the total mass in kilograms.
(b) A $3.48\text{ kg}$ bag of rice is shared equally among $6$ containers. What mass is in each container, in grams?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $9\times375=3375\text{ g}$ of contents.
$3375+240=3615\text{ g}$ altogether.
$3615\div1000=3.615\text{ kg}$.
(b) $3.48\text{ kg}=3480\text{ g}$.
$3480\div6=580\text{ g}$ in each container.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A grocer has $7.6\text{ kg}$ of nuts and fills $16$ bags of $425\text{ g}$ each. How much remains?
(b) Three identical crates and a $170\text{ kg}$ pallet have total mass $1.19\text{ t}$. Find the mass of each crate.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $7.6\text{ kg}=7600\text{ g}$.
$16\times425=6800\text{ g}$ used.
$7600-6800=800\text{ g}$ remains.
(b) $1.19\text{ t}=1190\text{ kg}$.
$1190-170=1020\text{ kg}$ for the three crates.
$1020\div3=340\text{ kg}$ for each crate.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A trailer has a load limit of $2.4\text{ t}$. It carries $1785\text{ kg}$ and another load of $690\text{ kg}$ is proposed. Can that load be added? Explain.
(b) Three parcels have masses $425\text{ g}$, $1.38\text{ kg}$ and $1.87\text{ kg}$. Delivery costs £6 per kilogram. Find the total delivery cost.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $2.4\text{ t}=2400\text{ kg}$.
$1785+690=2475\text{ kg}$.
$2475-2400=75\text{ kg}$ over the limit.
**No**, the load cannot be added.
(b) $425\text{ g}=0.425\text{ kg}$.
$0.425+1.38+1.87=3.675\text{ kg}$.
$3.675\times6=22.05$.
The total delivery cost is **£22.05**.

foundation.question_text:
Find the total mass of $600\text{ g}$ and $1.4\text{ kg}$.
Give the answer in kilograms.

A $3\text{ kg}$ bag has $850\text{ g}$ removed.
What mass remains?
Which is heavier: $1250\text{ g}$ or $1.3\text{ kg}$, and by how much?
foundation.solution_text:
$1.3\text{ kg}=1300\text{ g}$
$1300-1250$
$=50\text{ g}$
$1.3\text{ kg}$ is heavier by $50\text{ g}$.

foundation.question_text:
Three parcels have masses $250\text{ g}$, $750\text{ g}$ and $2\text{ kg}$.
Find their total mass.
foundation.solution_text:
$250\text{ g}+750\text{ g}=1000\text{ g}$
$=1\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ kg}+2\text{ kg}$
$=3\text{ kg}$

foundation.question_text:
A crate holds $8$ packets, each of mass $250\text{ g}$.
Find the total mass in kilograms.

A van can carry $1\text{ t}$.
It is loaded with $620\text{ kg}$.
How much capacity remains?

development.question_text:
A recipe uses $1.2\text{ kg}$ of flour and $350\text{ g}$ of sugar.
Find the combined mass in grams.

A parcel initially has mass $5.6\text{ kg}$.
Packaging of mass $425\text{ g}$ is removed.
Give the new mass in kilograms.

A pallet contains $12$ boxes of mass $15\text{ kg}$ each and a base of mass $35\text{ kg}$.
Find the total mass in tonnes.
development.solution_text:
$12\times15\text{ kg}$
$=180\text{ kg}$
$180\text{ kg}+35\text{ kg}$
$=215\text{ kg}$
$=0.215\text{ t}$

development.question_text:
A truck has a mass limit of $4.5\text{ t}$.
Its current mass is $3820\text{ kg}$.
Can another $750\text{ kg}$ load be added?
development.solution_text:
$4.5\text{ t}=4500\text{ kg}$
$3820\text{ kg}+750\text{ kg}$
$=4570\text{ kg}$
$4570>4500$, so the load cannot be added.

development.question_text:
A $2\text{ kg}$ bag of rice is divided equally into $5$ containers.
What mass is in each container in grams?

A market stall sold $3.25\text{ kg}$ of apples in the morning and $2750\text{ g}$ in the afternoon.
How many kilograms were sold altogether?

mastery.question_text:
A lift can carry $0.75\text{ t}$.
Four people have masses $82\text{ kg}$, $74\text{ kg}$, $91\text{ kg}$ and $68\text{ kg}$, and their equipment has mass $460\text{ kg}$.
Is the load within the limit?
mastery.solution_text:
$82+74+91+68$
$=315\text{ kg}$
$315\text{ kg}+460\text{ kg}$
$=775\text{ kg}$
$0.75\text{ t}=750\text{ kg}$
The load exceeds the limit by $25\text{ kg}$.

mastery.question_text:
A grocer has $9.5\text{ kg}$ of nuts.
After filling $18$ bags of $450\text{ g}$ each, how much remains?
mastery.solution_text:
$18\times450\text{ g}$
$=8100\text{ g}$
$=8.1\text{ kg}$
$9.5\text{ kg}-8.1\text{ kg}$
$=1.4\text{ kg}$

mastery.question_text:
Two identical crates and a $140\text{ kg}$ pallet have a total mass of $0.86\text{ t}$.
Find the mass of each crate.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.86\text{ t}=860\text{ kg}$
$860\text{ kg}-140\text{ kg}$
$=720\text{ kg}$
$720\div2\text{ kg}$
$=360\text{ kg}$
